correctness.rationale: For each edge, a one-hot categorical vector is negatively associated by a direct covariance factorization; independent-edge closure and disjoint decreasing color-specific acyclicity maps yield negative association of missing indicators. Pairwise covariance and a Chernoff moment bound give the universal upper and concentration inequalities. Conditioning on self-loop labels makes the conditional mean exactly (q/a) times the empty-bin count, whose variance is V=s a+s(s-1)b-s^2a^2. Total variance gives the exact lower bound. With the externally proved q~c s^(-1/3), a→e^(-1), V/s→e^(-1)-2e^(-2), the displayed limiting constants follow. Exhaustive exact rational enumeration verifies s=2,3, and no finite check is substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: The source full text establishes only the one-color DAG probability and first-moment asymptotics, whereas this statement gives a finite-size two-sided variance bound with a strictly positive loop-occupancy lower mechanism and an almost-sure law on the missing-count scale. Classical negative association covers the upper mechanism and is not claimed new. Both the conditional variance obstruction and its explicit asymptotic constant were compared with the source text and targeted published-finding corpus queries. Searches are not proof of priority and the simplicity of the underlying conditioning is acknowledged.
residual_risks: An unlocated general dependent-occupancy theorem may dominate the loop-conditioned variance bound.

value.rationale: The motivating paper determines an order-s^(2/3) mean deficit but only a law of large numbers for N_s/s. The new theorem gives exponentially summable deviations at the actual deficit scale, and a positive order-s^(1/3) lower bound on variance, isolating unavoidable fluctuations created by loop-label occupancy. This is a motivated structural fluctuation constraint rather than an arbitrary numerical slice; neither exponent is declared sharp and the lower mechanism is nontrivial even when negative association furnishes upper control.
